fabs.name: Semiconductor Complex Limited (SCL)
fabs.operator: Ministry of Electronics & IT, Govt. of India
fabs.newsQuery: Semiconductor Complex Limited SCL Mohali India
fabs.brief: India's oldest operational semiconductor fab, run directly by the Ministry of Electronics & IT. Specializes in custom ASICs at 180nm for ISRO's satellite payloads and DRDO's defense systems. Not commercially oriented — its output goes almost entirely into India's strategic space and defense programs.

fabs.name: SPEL Semiconductor
fabs.brief: One of India's oldest private-sector semiconductor facilities, focused on outsourced assembly, testing, and packaging (OSAT). Takes bare dies manufactured elsewhere and packages them into final chip form — a critical step in the semiconductor supply chain. Serves automotive and consumer electronics customers.

fabs.name: Micron Semiconductor ATP Facility
fabs.techNode: Assembly, Test & Packaging — DRAM & NAND Flash
fabs.newsQuery: Micron Technology semiconductor India Sanand Gujarat
fabs.brief: Micron's first semiconductor facility in India, inaugurated in February 2026. Assembles, tests, and packages DRAM and NAND flash memory chips for smartphones, laptops, servers, and automotive systems. Micron is the world's third-largest memory chip maker and one of the first foreign-owned semiconductor plants to go live under India's semiconductor mission.

fabs.name: Tata Electronics / PSMC Fab
fabs.newsQuery: Tata Electronics PSMC semiconductor fab Dholera India
fabs.brief: India's most ambitious true semiconductor fab — a 300mm AI-enabled wafer fabrication plant targeting 50,000 wafer starts per month at 28nm–110nm nodes. A special economic zone was notified in April 2026. Jointly developed with Taiwan's PSMC. First silicon is targeted for late 2026, primarily serving automotive, industrial, and consumer electronics markets.

fabs.name: CG Power / Renesas OSAT
fabs.operator: CG Power (India) + Renesas Electronics (Japan) + Stars Microelectronics (Thailand)
fabs.newsQuery: CG Power Renesas semiconductor fab India
fabs.brief: India's first full-service OSAT provider, inaugurated in August 2025. A tri-nation joint venture between India's CG Power, Japan's Renesas, and Thailand's Stars Microelectronics. The G1 facility handles around 0.5 million chip units per day and is scaling toward full commercial capacity. Produces analog and power management chips essential for automotive and industrial systems.

fabs.name: Kaynes Semicon OSAT
fabs.brief: Inaugurated in March 2026 with a production capacity of around 6 million chips per day. Kaynes Technology specializes in high-reliability chip packaging for sectors where failure is not an option — automotive, medical, and aerospace. Advanced packaging technologies like system-in-package (SiP) can combine multiple chips into a single compact, high-performance module.

fabs.name: ISMC Analog Fab
fabs.newsQuery: ISMC semiconductor fab India Karnataka Mysuru
fabs.brief: A proposed analog semiconductor fab originally backed by UAE-based Next Orbit Ventures in consortium with Tower Semiconductor (Israel). The project stalled after the primary investor withdrew and Intel's acquisition of Tower fell through. The Indian government is actively working to revive it, as a 65nm analog fab would complement the logic fabs being built in Gujarat.

fabs.name: HCL – Foxconn OSAT
fabs.capacity: WLP display driver IC packaging (volume TBD)
fabs.newsQuery: HCL Foxconn semiconductor OSAT India Jewar
fabs.brief: A joint venture between HCL and Foxconn for semiconductor assembly and testing near the upcoming Noida International Airport, approved by Cabinet in May 2025. Notably focused on wafer-level packaging (WLP) of display driver ICs — an advanced technique not previously adopted by any India OSAT. Foxconn owns a 40% stake. Proximity to a major air cargo hub is deliberate, as chips move by air.

fabs.name: CDIL Semiconductors Expansion
fabs.newsQuery: CDIL Continental Device India semiconductor Mohali expansion
fabs.brief: CDIL is one of India's oldest private semiconductor manufacturers (founded 1964), now expanding its Mohali plant under the India Semiconductor Mission. The expansion targets high-power discrete devices — MOSFETs, IGBTs, and SiC components used in solar inverters, EV powertrains, and industrial motor drives. Annual capacity will grow from 600 million to over 760 million units.

fabs.name: RIR Power Electronics SiC Fab
fabs.capacity: SiC wafer epitaxy — phased rollout from 2026
fabs.newsQuery: RIR Power Electronics silicon carbide semiconductor Odisha Bhubaneswar
fabs.brief: India's first Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor fabrication plant, backed by the Odisha state government. SiC chips handle far higher voltages and temperatures than conventional silicon, making them essential for EV inverters, solar converters, and industrial power grids. SiC wafer epitaxy production targeted from 2026 with phased commercial rollout.

fabs.name: Crystal Matrix GaN / MicroLED Fab
fabs.capacity: 72,000 sq. m of GaN display panels/year (target)
fabs.newsQuery: Crystal Matrix GaN microLED semiconductor Dholera India
fabs.brief: India's first Gallium Nitride (GaN) based mini/micro-LED display fabrication facility, approved by Cabinet in May 2026. GaN enables displays far brighter, more energy-efficient, and longer-lasting than OLED or LCD — the technology behind next-gen TVs, AR/VR headsets, and automotive dashboards. Will produce 6-inch GaN wafers and full display modules, targeting 72,000 sq. metres of panels annually.

fabs.name: Tata Electronics ATMP
fabs.techNode: Wire Bond, Flip Chip & Integrated Systems Packaging (ISP)
fabs.newsQuery: Tata Electronics semiconductor ATMP Assam Morigaon Jagiroad
fabs.brief: Tata Electronics' massive ATMP facility in Assam, with a foundation laid in August 2024. At full capacity it will produce 48 million semiconductor chips per day and create over 30,000 jobs — the largest employment footprint of any semiconductor facility in India. Focuses on wire bond, flip chip, and advanced integrated systems packaging (ISP), targeting AI, industrial, and consumer electronics markets.

fabs.name: Sahasra Semiconductors OSAT
fabs.newsQuery: Sahasra Semiconductors Bhiwadi Rajasthan semiconductor OSAT
fabs.brief: India's first SME-led semiconductor ATMP/OSAT facility, inaugurated in May 2026 — making Rajasthan the newest state on India's semiconductor map. Operates outside the ISM framework, under the SPECS scheme. Already exporting ~60% of production to the US, Germany, France, and Eastern Europe. Initial capacity of 60 million units per year, expanding to 400–600 million units over 2–3 years.

fabs.name: Suchi Semicon OSAT
fabs.newsQuery: Suchi Semicon SSPL semiconductor Surat Gujarat India
fabs.brief: Approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2026 as part of a ₹3,936 crore dual-project approval alongside Crystal Matrix. Suchi Semicon will set up an OSAT facility in Surat for discrete semiconductor manufacturing, with a production capacity of over 1 billion chips per year. Targets power electronics, analog ICs, and industrial systems for automotive and consumer markets.

fabs.name: 3D Glass Solutions Advanced Packaging
fabs.capacity: 3D glass substrate packages for AI/5G (volume TBD)
fabs.newsQuery: 3D Glass Solutions semiconductor Odisha Bhubaneswar packaging
fabs.brief: India's first advanced 3D glass substrate semiconductor packaging unit, with groundbreaking held in April 2026 at Info Valley, Bhubaneswar. Run by Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions (HIPSPL), the Indian subsidiary of US-based 3D Glass Solutions. Glass substrates allow chips to be stacked and interconnected in three dimensions — critical for AI accelerators and high-performance computing where silicon interposers are too expensive or too limited.
